sections.title: Instructions for Sound Teaching
observations: Paul emphasizes the importance of sound doctrine and teaching within the church. He instructs Titus to teach what is appropriate for different groups within the church, including older men, older women, younger women, younger men, and slaves. This highlights the need for tailored teaching that addresses the specific needs and responsibilities of each group.

sections.title: The Role of Grace in Christian Living
observations: Paul reminds Titus that the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people. This grace not only saves but also instructs believers to live godly lives, turning away from ungodliness and worldly passions. This section emphasizes the transformative power of grace in the life of a believer.

sections.title: The Hope of Eternal Life
observations: The chapter concludes with a reminder of the hope that believers have in Christ's return. Paul encourages Titus to proclaim these truths confidently, reinforcing the importance of living in light of the hope of eternal life. This hope should motivate believers to live righteously and to be zealous for good works.

importantVerses.commentary: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, teaching us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age.
Who gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people for his own possession who are zealous for good works.

questions: What does it mean to teach sound doctrine in a way that is relevant to different groups within the church?
How does the grace of God transform our lives and instruct us in godliness?
In what ways can we be zealous for good works as a response to the grace we have received?
